schema.title: System map
schema.intro: This page shows how the site's money records move between states. It reads its shape from the same code the site runs, so it updates itself whenever the real rules change. Nothing here is linked to a real payment.
schema.list.heading: What can happen next
schema.list.none: Nothing. This state is an ending.
schema.legend.heading: Who can move a record:
schema.widget.hint: Choose a state to see its ways forward.
schema.check.heading: Live check
schema.check.intro: The machines above promise some combinations can never be stored. This check looks for them in this site's own records.
schema.check.none: All stored payment records fit the rules.
schema.check.armed_without_claim: A refund is set to send, but no job holds this row.
schema.check.claim_without_charge: A job holds this row, but its payment has no charge record.
schema.refund.title: A refund at the payment provider
schema.refund.intro: Each refund the site owes a buyer lives in one record. The record says where the money is and who needs to act next. A refund always sits in exactly one of the states below.
schema.refund.state.ready.detail: Everything checks out. The site can send this refund to the provider.
schema.refund.state.send_armed.detail: The site has sent, or may have sent, the refund to the provider. It waits for proof of what happened. It will not send twice.
schema.refund.state.observing.detail: The provider has not given a final answer yet. The site checks again later and never sends another refund.
schema.refund.state.check.detail: The provider's answer did not settle things. The site must check it again. It will not send another refund.
schema.refund.state.choice_open.detail: The site cannot know what happened. You check the provider and say what is true.
schema.refund.state.choice_not_sent: Your decision needed: nothing was sent
schema.refund.state.choice_not_sent.deta: The provider shows the refund was never sent. You confirm this, and the site can safely try again.
schema.refund.state.choice_returned: Your decision needed: some money is back
schema.refund.state.choice_returned.deta: The provider returned part of the money. You confirm the part that came back. The site will not offer to send it again, because that could pay the returned part twice.
schema.refund.state.returned: Money back: record it in Money
schema.refund.state.returned.detail: The provider returned the money. Record it in Money, then this refund is done.
schema.refund.state.recorded.detail: The money is back and written down. Nothing more is needed.
schema.refund.edge.observe: The provider has not answered yet
schema.refund.edge.replay: The site safely tries the same send again
schema.refund.edge.proved_not_sent: Proof arrives that nothing was sent
schema.refund.edge.provider_returned: The provider proves the money is back
schema.refund.edge.conflict_returned: Provider evidence: some or all of the money is back
schema.refund.edge.owner_confirms_return: You confirm the money came back
schema.review.title: A payment row kept for review
schema.review.intro: Sometimes the site keeps a payment row because its records disagree. Each reason has one kind of proof that clears it.
schema.review.state.none.detail: The row's records agree, or it holds no open question. Nothing needs your attention.
schema.review.state.open.detail: The records disagree in one exact way. The row waits until the matching proof arrives. You can mark it seen without clearing it.
schema.review.state.seen.detail: You have looked at this disagreement. The row still waits for the same proof.
schema.review.reason.partially_returned_: Part of the money came back, part is still owed
schema.review.evidence.unique_reference: Proof arrives that each booking has its own payment
schema.review.evidence.all_returned_and_: Proof arrives that all the money is back and written down
schema.row.title: One payment row's held work
schema.row.intro: Every payment has a row. The row can be held by a refund run, wait for the owner to look at a problem, or remember returned money the books do not show yet. This map shows every mix of those and how each one ends.
schema.row.state.free.detail: No work is held on this row. It can be claimed by a refund run, or record how a checkout ended.
schema.row.state.claim.detail: A refund run is working on this row's money right now. Nothing may delete or merge this person until the run lets go.
schema.row.state.review.detail: The owner still has to look at a payment problem on this row. Deleting waits; a merge carries the problem across.
schema.row.state.unrecorded.detail: This person's money went back, but the accounts do not show it yet. Deleting waits until it is recorded.
schema.row.state.claim_review.detail: A refund run holds the row while a problem also waits for the owner. The run's hold is named first.
schema.row.state.claim_unrecorded: Held, money not in the books
schema.row.state.claim_unrecorded.detail: A refund run holds the row while returned money is still off the books.
schema.row.state.review_unrecorded: Owner waiting, money not in the books
schema.row.state.review_unrecorded.detai: A problem waits for the owner and returned money is still off the books. The owner's problem is named first.
schema.row.state.claim_review_unrecorded: Held, with both kinds of work
A refund run holds the row while a problem waits for the owner and returned money is off the books.
schema.row.state.settled.detail: This payment ended and the row only remembers the outcome. It holds up nothing.
schema.row.edge.claim_granted: A refund run takes the row
schema.row.edge.settle_release: The run finishes and lets go
schema.row.edge.settle_found_unrecorded: The run finds money the books do not show
schema.row.edge.settle_open_partially_re: The run finds money only partly returned
schema.row.edge.settle_open_shared_refer: The run finds two rows sharing one payment
schema.row.edge.settle_retire_partially_: All the money is returned and recorded
schema.row.edge.settle_retire_shared_ref: The payment is one row's own again
schema.row.edge.write_outcome: The checkout ends and the row remembers how
